title.narrative: COVID-19: Response for Affected Poor and Vulnerable Groups Project

description.narrative: The project aims to address the needs of poor and vulnerable groups affected by the coronavirus disease (COVID-19). It will take a comprehensive approach to address the complex and varying levels of vulnerabilities affecting marginalized populations. All outputs are aligned with the common objective of improving the capability of vulnerable groups to withstand the impacts of COVID-19 by providing immediate assistance to these groups while positioning them to achieve higher levels of economic and social well-being post-COVID-19. The project will (i) respond to the immediate physical, mental, social, and environmental needs of home-bound older people and persons with disabilities (PWD) who are highly vulnerable to COVID-19; (ii) boost local food security and help smallholder agriculture producers generate income; and (iii) help address family and gender-based violence.

Victims of family and GBV increased reporting to authorities Progress/Status: Ongoing.
Observations from training with police officers: increase in FPA/domestic violence calls, from a few per week to multiple times daily, suggests more awareness and increased utilization of the FPA.
The prevalence of repeat FPA/domestic violence calls to the same households highlights a systemic challenge for law enforcement, particularly given limited staffing, and impacts response effectiveness. Output: Food security and income generating support delivered to small agricultural producers Indicator: At least 300 women farmers on Babeldoab Island receive accessible agriculture production support to expand their taro production Achievement: 249 Progress/Status: Total of 941 women farmers have received production support to expand their taro production.
Of which 233 are women are from the 20 women groups/farmer cooperatives that have been awarded seed grant with memorandum of agreements signed with Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Environment, Bureau of Agriculture.
Additional 708 individual women farmers are receiving project support (383 from BOA, 148 from PCC-CRE, 177 from TTM).
Support provided includes seedlings, trainings on farm techniques (soil management, farm mapping, etc.) business integrity and compliance (getting license, record keeping, ICT, etc.)
The project facilitates broader engagement of supported women in other initiatives such as digital village, initiatives to support their involvement in entering supply chain.
Food processing center continues to purchase of taro from project-supported women cooperatives (buy back scheme of 50% women produce)
Data Source: BOA baseline assessment (Q2 2020); M&E firm's project completion report (Q2 2026); PMU quarterly monitoring and progress reports; and ADB project missions
